nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be differentiable at $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$. Then for every row index $i$ and column index $j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the $i$-th coordinate of $Df(x)\, e_j$, where $Df(x)$ is the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ and $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$.
nodes.title: Jacobian entries at a point of differentiability

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$. For every row index $i$ and column index $j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the derivative at $t = 0$ of $t \mapsto f_i(x + t e_j)$, where $f_i$ is the $i$-th component of $f$ and $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$. This derivative is taken to be $0$ when it does not exist.
nodes.title: Entries of the Jacobian matrix are partial derivatives

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$, $g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^p$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and write $J_h(y)$ for the Jacobian matrix of $h$ at $y$. If $f$ is differentiable at $x$ and $g$ is differentiable at $f(x)$, then $J_{g \circ f}(x) = J_g(f(x))\, J_f(x)$, a product of a $p \times n$ and an $n \times m$ matrix.
nodes.title: Chain rule for Jacobian matrices

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be differentiable at $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$. Then the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the matrix, in the standard bases of $\mathbb{R}^m$ and $\mathbb{R}^n$, of the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$, viewed as a linear map $\mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: The Jacobian is the matrix of the derivative

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a real $n \times m$ matrix. At every point $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the Jacobian matrix of the map $y \mapsto M y$ from $\mathbb{R}^m$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $M$.
nodes.title: Jacobian of a linear map given by a matrix

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be differentiable at $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and let $J$ be the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$. Then for every $v \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the product $J v$ equals $Df(x)\, v$, the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ applied to $v$.
nodes.title: The Jacobian matrix computes the derivative

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the Jacobian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the $n \times m$ real matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is the partial derivative of the $i$-th component $f_i$ of $f$ in the $j$-th coordinate direction at $x$: the derivative at $t = 0$ of $t \mapsto f_i(x + t e_j)$, where $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$.
